goal: The ledger's posting job looks at each store's book in a rotating order (ledger_books.checked_at), skips a book with nothing new and looks at an idle one hourly, and keeps a book whose turn stopped short listed: the third of three books is reached within three runs, and the ledger job reads at most 10 more rows per added store on an idle tick.
why: runLedgerPosting() orders the books by updated_at, which only the owner's edits move, so a busy book first in the list takes the whole 40-second budget every run and the books behind it never get their turn; and every book is listed on every five-minute tick even when nothing new was issued. After the step the order rotates, an idle book costs nothing between hourly looks, and Kaizena Flow's own books are a book in the same list.

depends_on.why: its query-budget.int.test.ts counts rows read per job with 1 and 20 stores (and holds runLedgerPosting()'s statements with 20 books); the done-when is read there and its baseline is lowered here

commits.title: Every book gets its turn, and an idle book is looked at hourly

changes.how: `ledgerBooks` (the table "ledger_books", line 18801 today) gains `checkedAt: timestamp("checked_at", { withTimezone: true })` (nullable; doc comment: 'When the ledger job last looked at the book: what was issued after it lists the book again.') and `behind: boolean("behind").notNull().default(false)` (doc comment: 'The last turn stopped before the book was caught up, so the job keeps it listed.'). No index: the table holds one row per store's book and the job reads it whole. Run `pnpm db:generate`; the generated migration must hold exactly the two `ADD COLUMN` statements. Tripletex's and Fiken's looked_at columns are step 3.23's, not this step's.

runLedgerPosting() (line 1038) and openLedgerBookEarlier() (line 174). (1) Next to DOCS_A_ROUND (line 487) add `/** How many entries a book compares with Tripletex in one go (compareWithTripletex()'s own default). */ const COMPARE_A_ROUND = 25;`. (2) Move the list statement out of runLedgerPosting() into an exported `ledgerBooksDue()` directly above it, with the doc comment 'The books the ledger job looks at, in their turn: open or closed in the last 60 days, and never looked at, behind, last looked at over an hour ago, or with a shop invoice or credit note issued since; the least recently looked at first.' It returns `typedRows(z.object({ id: col.uuid, store_id: col.uuid, currency: col.currency, opened_on: col.text, closed_on: col.textOrNull, listed_at: col.text }), sql`...`)` for exactly this statement: select b.id, b.store_id, b.currency, b.opened_on::text, b.closed_on::text, now()::text as listed_at from commerce.ledger_books b where (b.closed_on is null or b.closed_on >= current_date - 60) and (b.checked_at is null or b.behind or b.checked_at < now() - interval '1 hour' or exists (select 1 from commerce.invoices i where i.store_id = b.store_id and i.issued_on >= (b.checked_at - interval '1 day')::date and i.issued_at > b.checked_at) or exists (select 1 from commerce.credit_notes c where c.store_id = b.store_id and c.issued_on >= (b.checked_at - interval '1 day')::date and c.issued_at > b.checked_at)) order by b.checked_at nulls first, b.id (the issued_on bound lets each exists() use invoices_issued_idx and credit_notes_issued_idx, both on (store_id, issued_on); issued_at decides). Add no other exists(): a card payment is captured as its invoice is issued (D159) and a refund is given with its credit note, so dueDocuments() takes them in the same turn; Work's documents, payments that change state later, payouts, dispute lines and a waiting document whose day is up have no index on (store_id, a time) or change state without a new row, and are taken at the hourly look (no ledger_waiting exists(): its rows are deleted only when the job posts them, line 1023, so a stale one would list its book on every tick). (3) In runLedgerPosting(), add `limit?: number` to its options (`options: { budgetMs?: number; limit?: number } = {}`, for the tests), `const limit = options.limit ?? DOCS_A_ROUND;`, read `const books = await ledgerBooksDue();`, and make the loop exactly: for (const book of books) { if (Date.now() > deadline) break; let behind = false; try { const r = await postDueDocuments(book.store_id, book, { limit, deadline }); posted += r.posted; waiting += r.waiting; /* Step 4: what is posted here, compared with what Tripletex holds for it. */ const c = book.closed_on === null ? (await compareWithTripletex(book.store_id, book, { deadline, limit: COMPARE_A_ROUND })).compared : 0; compared += c; /* Stopped short (the round's limit, the comparison's, or the deadline): the book stays listed until it is caught up. */ behind = r.posted + r.waiting >= limit || c >= COMPARE_A_ROUND || Date.now() > deadline; done += 1; } catch (error) { log("error", "ledger.posting_failed", { storeId: book.store_id, bookId: book.id }, error); } /* A caught-up book is marked with the list's time, so anything issued after the list lists it again; a behind one with its turn's end, so the books caught up in this run come before it next time. A turn that threw is not behind: it is tried again at the hourly look. */ await db().execute(sql`update commerce.ledger_books set checked_at = case when ${behind}::boolean then now() else ${book.listed_at}::timestamptz end, behind = ${behind}::boolean where id = ${book.id}::uuid and store_id = ${book.store_id}::uuid`); } (write the /* */ comments as // line comments in the code). Books the loop did not reach keep their checked_at and come first next run. Do not touch updated_at: the owner's edits move it. Leave the bank matching after the loop as it is. (4) openLedgerBookEarlier(): its statement `update commerce.ledger_books set opened_on = ${openedOn}::date, updated_at = now()` (line 191) becomes `update commerce.ledger_books set opened_on = ${openedOn}::date, behind = true, updated_at = now()`, so the days it adds are posted from the next tick, not the hourly look.

I opened ledger.ts runLedgerPosting() at 1038: it orders by updated_at, which the job never moves (CR-16), and postDueDocuments() (line 995) posts at most DOCS_A_ROUND documents or until the deadline. Corrected for the split: Tripletex's and Fiken's looked_at columns moved to step 3.23 with their own migration. Found while splitting: the old text set checked_at after every turn, so a book cut short by the budget or the round's limit would leave its backlog to the hourly look (a newly opened book's history would post 40 seconds an hour instead of every five minutes); the behind column keeps such a book listed at the back of the order. The old list of exists() tables left out Work's invoices, credit notes, payments and losses and the dispute lines that dueDocuments() also reads; they are named now under the same index rule. Review (12 November): that index rule, taken literally, dropped every exists() (no table has an index on (store_id, issued_at or created_at); invoices and credit notes have (store_id, issued_on), schema.ts 6855 and 6946), and insert times miss documents that become due by a change of state (a payment captured later, a refund that succeeds, a payout paid); so only the two shop tables keep an exists(), bounded by issued_on, and the rest wait for the hourly look. The ledger_waiting exists() is dropped (keyed by store, not book, and its rows outlive their documents). checked_at for a caught-up book is the list's now(), not the turn's end, so nothing issued during a turn is missed; the comparison's 25-entry limit counts as cut; openLedgerBookEarlier() sets behind; a turn that threw is not behind; ledger_books_checked_idx is dropped (a one-row-per-book table). ledger_books.store_id is not null (schema.ts 135): Kaizena Flow's books are its own store's (D467), in the same list with no special case.
